- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.25) and price is trending upward, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with momentum.
- Model frequently overcorrects after strong downward moves — if recent sentiment is negative and price drops, forecast should be slightly below true value to avoid overbought reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile — apply 1–2% downward adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model may misread trend direction — use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
- When sentiment is flat (0.25–0.75) and price is near mean, model often drifts — apply mean reversion correction: forecast = previous 10-day average ± 1–2% based on volatility.
